summary: A trail of links showing where the current page sits in a hierarchy, built from a navigation landmark and an ordered list (a family of Web Components).

label.note: Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Translate it, and make it unique when a page has several navigation landmarks.

anatomy.name: nav
anatomy.notes: Native nav element in the shadow root; the landmark.

accessibility.role: navigation (landmark) containing a list of listitems
accessibility.accessibleNameSource: label prop as aria-label on the inner nav; link text for links.

keyboard.Tab: moves through the links in order

aria: inner nav has aria-label from label
list host: role=list; item host: role=listitem; set when the element connects, before it renders

current page: inner span with role=link, aria-disabled=true and aria-current=page; Chromium drops aria-current from a generic node, so the role is what exposes it (checked in the accessibility tree); it has no href and is not focusable
separator host: role=presentation and aria-hidden=true, so only items count in the list
ellipsis: icon hidden, label read as text (not aria-hidden, unlike the reference)
accessibility.targetSize: Links in the trail are inline text and fall under the WCAG 2.5.8 inline exception.

coverage: accessibility tree: one list whose semantic children are exactly the steps
separators presentation and aria-hidden, absent from the tree
list and item roles set before first render, no flicker
current page: disabled, unfocusable link node with aria-current=page
links with href, tab order, Enter follows
solid focus ring on keyboard focus only
link, page and hover colors in light and dark
ellipsis label read, icon hidden, 36px box

openQuestions.question: How do ol and li semantics survive custom element boundaries?
openQuestions.recommendation: Hosts carry role=list and role=listitem; shadow roots hold only slots. Verify in the accessibility tree.
openQuestions.answer: Host roles, checked in the accessibility tree by the spec.

openQuestions.question: Current page: plain span with aria-current, or a disabled link role?
openQuestions.recommendation: A span with role=link, aria-disabled and aria-current=page: the accessibility tree prunes aria-current from a generic span (verified), and the link role is the pattern the trail pattern allows.
openQuestions.answer: role=link with aria-disabled=true and aria-current=page, not focusable.

openQuestions.question: Ellipsis hidden from assistive technology with a hidden label (reference), or announced?
openQuestions.recommendation: Announced with its label: hidden content cannot be read, so the visible dots would be an unexplained gap.

href.note: Link address. Without it the element renders an anchor without href, which is not focusable or a link. javascript:, vbscript: and data: URLs are dropped: the link renders without href and a console warning names it (SB-0115).
